discovery: Invention and development of the optical lattice clock

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Katori conceived the optical lattice clock: neutral atoms confined in an optical lattice tuned to a 'magic' wavelength, so that the trap leaves the clock transition unperturbed while thousands of atoms are interrogated in the Lamb-Dicke regime. Ye turned the concept into the world's most accurate and stable clocks. His group reached fractional uncertainties near 10^-18 and below, controlled many-body interactions in degenerate Fermi gases, and resolved the gravitational redshift across a single millimetre-scale atomic sample. Together their work has improved timekeeping by more than two orders of magnitude, driving the redefinition of the SI second. It has also opened new tests of general relativity and searches for dark matter and variations of fundamental constants, and it makes relativistic geodesy possible. Their clocks created a new measurement paradigm, joining quantum control of atoms to fundamental tests of gravity.
